newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 12.0/12.5 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 12.0/12.5 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 12.0/12.5 percent on Monday morning, with the focus on the new bank reserve requirement rate which becomes effective on Wednesday, dealers said.
They said overnight liquidity appeared to be well balanced but worries were seen in one-week money, suggesting concern on the implication of the new rate on the money market after Wednesday.
The new reserve rate will be five percent from the current three percent. Some operators anticipated a drain of five to eight trillion rupiah from the market.
One local bank dealer said worries were not so prevalent in overnight money, but people were bidding for one-week money and longer-term swaps were also trending upward.
"It seems that people don't know how the market is going to be affected after the new rate. They are trying to boost reserves at present," the dealer said.
One-week money was traded at 13.50/13.75 percent and two at 14.00/14.25 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Friday was 11.52 percent, compared with 9.76 percent on Thursday.
Bond dealers said the market was quiet, with the yield for PLN V/A bonds staying at 14.9 percent.
